sentences.zh: 我不是——Bryce，你有什么回应吗？

sentences.zh: 很多对话都在讨论更倾向于其他语言，所以不清楚为什么我同意切换语言很困难，

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, very, very simple answer about why not only I want to save C++, but everybody should want to save C++.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，关于为什么不仅我想拯救C++，而且每个人都应该想要拯救C++，答案非常非常简单。

sentences.en: I'm lazy, and, and, and I hope everybody else is lazy, too.
sentences.zh: 我很懒，而且，而且，我希望其他人也一样懒。

sentences.en: C++ has one of the largest bodies of existing written code out there, and, um, if C++ becomes a sunset language, um, over time, that code is going to get harder.
sentences.zh: C++拥有现存最大的代码库之一，而且，嗯，如果C++变成一种日落语言，嗯，随着时间的推移，维护这些代码会变得越来越难。

sentences.en: It's harder and harder to maintain, and eventually, inevitably, large amounts of that code will have to be rewritten entirely in a different language.
sentences.zh: 维护难度会越来越大，最终，不可避免地，大量代码将不得不完全用另一种语言重写。

sentences.en: Um, and there's just no world in which that, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且根本不存在那种，嗯，

sentences.en: that, um, that migration does not come with a grave cost, um, and I, I don't want to, I don't want it to pay that cost.
sentences.zh: 那种，嗯，那种迁移不会带来沉重代价的世界，嗯，我，我不想，我不想付出那个代价。

sentences.en: I would like to be able to, I would like the world to be able to continue using C++ code for the next 50, 60 years and have it be a healthy part of the ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 我希望能够，我希望世界在未来50、60年里能够继续使用C++代码，并使其成为生态系统中健康的一部分。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that every new project should be written in C++.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说每个新项目都应该用C++编写。

sentences.en: Um, I think there are some that should be, um, but I don't want existing, the existing body of code to have to be rewritten or replaced because that, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为有些项目应该用，嗯，但我不想让现有的，现有的代码库不得不被重写或替换，因为那个，呃，

sentences.en: if we do that only because, if we have to do that solely because the C++ language, um, has become stagnant, uh, that would be a huge waste.
sentences.zh: 如果我们仅仅因为，如果我们不得不这样做仅仅是因为C++语言，嗯，变得停滞不前，呃，那将是巨大的浪费。

sentences.en: Um, and I, I, you know, you get, you, you, you, you, a lot of people get excited about, like, rewriting a project from scratch.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我，我，你知道，你得到，你，你，你，很多人对从零开始重写一个项目感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Um, like, starting over, you know, oh, we can do everything right this time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像，重新开始，你知道，哦，这次我们可以把一切都做对。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不想那样做。

sentences.en: That just sounds like a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 那听起来工作量太大了。

sentences.en: And I, I would much rather work, um, smart, uh, than hard.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我宁愿工作，嗯，聪明一点，呃，而不是辛苦一点。

sentences.en: And I, I, I think it's really good to be lazy in this field, um, and to, to not reinvent the wheel.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我，我真的认为在这个领域懒一点很好，嗯，而且，不要重复造轮子。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, that's, that's why I think we should want to save C++ because like it's here today and we have a ton of code written in it and that code is important.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道，这就是，这就是为什么我认为我们应该想要拯救C++，因为它今天就在这里，我们有大量用它编写的代码，而且这些代码很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And your answer kind of highlights why, uh, three of the four main successor initiatives, although I guess you might not consider circle a successor initiative,
sentences.zh: 你的回答在某种程度上突显了为什么，呃，四个主要继任者计划中的三个，虽然我想你可能不认为Circle是一个继任者计划，

sentences.en: but it's always listed in the liSt.
sentences.zh: 但它总是出现在名单上。

sentences.zh: CPP Front，基本上你可以，你知道，CPP2只是，或者CPP Front编译成C++。

sentences.en: C++ everything works.

sentences.en: Carbon has like a first class story for trying to interrupt and they're trying to build tools for where it won't work.
sentences.zh: Carbon有一个一流的故事，试图进行互操作，他们正在为无法工作的地方构建工具。

sentences.en: And circle is just a advanced C++ state of the art compiler.
sentences.zh: 而Circle只是一个先进的、最先进的C++编译器。

sentences.en: I think Val, which also we got another, uh, comment.
sentences.zh: 我认为Val，我们也收到了另一条，呃，评论。

sentences.en: Ooh, let's bring up my LinkedIn because I'll mention them by name as well, except I need to switch back to, uh, Chrome now.
sentences.zh: 哦，把我的LinkedIn调出来，因为我也要提他们的名字，不过我现在需要切回，呃，Chrome。

sentences.en: So I don't need to sign in.
sentences.zh: 所以我不需要登录。

sentences.zh: 我收到了一条评论，说你提到了Val，它现在不叫Val了。

sentences.en: We need to start calling it by its real name.
sentences.zh: 我们需要开始用它的真名来称呼它。

sentences.en: This was Chris Van Renz, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我想这是Chris Van Renz写的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the new name for it was, is Hilo.
sentences.zh: 它的新名字是，Hilo。

sentences.zh: 所以我们肯定会口误叫它Val。

sentences.en: And I, I thought about going back and renaming our episodes because while we were talking, uh, with Sean Perrin, when we were in Folkston in the UK for CPP on C,
sentences.zh: 而且我，我考虑过回去重命名我们的剧集，因为当我们和Sean Perrin交谈时，呃，我们在英国Folkston参加CPP on C时，

sentences.en: it was still named Val.
sentences.zh: 它还叫Val。

sentences.en: But then by the time I think some of those episodes came out or right after it got renamed to Hilo, we're, we're leaving it as Val back there.
sentences.zh: 但后来我想在其中一些剧集发布时，或者就在那之后，它被重命名为Hilo，我们把那里的名字留作Val。

sentences.en: But going forward, we will try to, uh, call it Hilo.
sentences.zh: 但展望未来，我们会尽量，呃，叫它Hilo。

sentences.en: But Hilo is really of the four of those initiatives, Circle, CPP Front, and Carbon.
sentences.zh: 但Hilo确实是这四个计划中，Circle、CPP Front和Carbon，

sentences.en: Hilo is the only one that isn't trying to prioritize backwards compat.
sentences.zh: Hilo是唯一一个不试图优先考虑向后兼容性的。

sentences.en: And I still think they are trying to have some kind of story, like they'll have a, you know, maybe a, from C++ to Hilo, you know, documentation.
sentences.zh: 而且我仍然认为他们试图讲某种故事，比如他们会有一个，你知道，也许是一个，从C++到Hilo的，你知道，文档。

sentences.en: But, um, the other three are all, all have really good stories.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，其他三个都有非常好的故事。

sentences.en: And a part of, and honestly, I'm not, I'm not sure if that's, uh, part of me thinks that that's a great idea to not focus on the backwards compatibility.
sentences.zh: 而且老实说，我不是，我不确定这是否，呃，我的一部分认为不关注向后兼容性是个好主意。

sentences.en: Um, and the reason being, it's real hard, uh, to be compatible with C++.
sentences.zh: 嗯，原因在于，与C++兼容真的很难，呃。

sentences.en: Part of me thinks, if you, if you don't focus on it from the start of the language, um, it'll never happen.
sentences.zh: 我的一部分认为，如果你，如果你从语言开始时不关注它，嗯，它就永远不会实现。

sentences.en: Um, but like, if you do focus on it from the start of the language, then it, it may consume your entire effort.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，如果你确实从语言开始时就关注它，那么它，它可能会消耗你所有的精力。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, there's a relevant story that I, that I tell Ramona all the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，有一个相关的故事，我，我一直告诉Ramona。

sentences.en: Um, uh, and, uh, I'm going to tell it, but I think Connor's going to speed it up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，而且，呃，我要讲出来，但我认为Connor会把它加速处理。

sentences.en: Well, we have to decide, uh, are we going to try, is, is, do you want your algorithm question to be a separate episode?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们得决定，呃，我们要尝试，是，是，你想把你的算法问题作为单独的一集吗？

sentences.en: Or are we going to try and squeeze it into the end of this discussion?
sentences.zh: 还是我们要尝试把它挤进这次讨论的最后？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.zh: 我让你来做决定。

sentences.zh: 怎么，好吧，你觉得需要多长时间？

sentences.en: 10 minutes?
sentences.zh: 10分钟？

sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道吗，我们，我们，我们，我们要，我们要跳过，我们要跳过Bryce的故事。

sentences.en: Okay, we'll skip the Bryce story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们跳过Bryce的故事。

sentences.en: That can be irresponsible, I bet.
sentences.zh: 我敢说那可能很不负责任。

sentences.en: But actually, what we're just talking about here, um, uh, brings up an interesting question, which I've never, I think, uh, thought about deeply before.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们刚才在这里谈论的内容，嗯，呃，提出了一个有趣的问题，我想我以前从未，呃，深入思考过。

sentences.en: But, um, I think it's something that both of us know to be true, which is C, C++ is a really poor interface language.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，我认为这是我们俩都知道是事实的事情，那就是C，C++是一种非常糟糕的接口语言。

sentences.en: Um, and by that, I mean, like, it is a, a poor language to be used as a medium for, uh, for other languages to interoperate with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，它是一种糟糕的语言，不能作为，呃，其他语言进行互操作的媒介。

sentences.en: Now, C, on the other hand, is frickin' great.
sentences.zh: 现在，C语言，另一方面，简直太棒了。

sentences.en: Um, like, C is, is the de facto, um, ABI language.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比如，C是事实上的，嗯，ABI语言。

sentences.en: Um, like, like, if you want to write a library, if you want to have two different, you know, languages or libraries or things interact, you, you define a, a, a C, um, uh, ABI.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比如，如果你想写一个库，如果你想让两种不同的，你知道，语言或库或事物进行交互，你，你定义一个，一个，一个C，嗯，呃，ABI。

sentences.en: Um, uh, or a C-API and then that has a C-A-B-I, um, and, you know, there's a number of reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，或者一个C-API，然后它有一个C-ABI，嗯，而且，你知道，这有几个原因。

sentences.en: One, the, um, the nature of C means that, um, you, you have less stuff boil up into, uh, the API that has, um, uh, uh,
sentences.zh: 第一，嗯，C的本质意味着，嗯，你，你更少的东西会冒泡到，呃，具有，嗯，呃，呃，

sentences.en: a platform-specific ABI nature to it.
sentences.zh: 平台特定ABI性质的API中。

sentences.en: Um, and I guess also, like, less of the type system is exposed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我想还有，比如，更少的类型系统被暴露出来。

sentences.en: Like, what, what else is it that makes C a better interface language than C++?
sentences.zh: 比如，还有什么让C成为比C++更好的接口语言？

sentences.en: Um, what do you think?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I think we know this to be true, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我们都知道这是事实，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it is the lingua franqua of FFI and, like, almost any language that builds an FFI, it's to target C.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是FFI的通用语，而且，比如，几乎任何构建FFI的语言，都是以C为目标的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't actually know.
sentences.zh: 我其实不知道。

sentences.en: And if you, and if you look at, like, ways of, like, interfacing between, like, C++ and Python, like, they're, at least the last time I did anything in that space,
sentences.zh: 而且如果你，如果你看看，比如，在C++和Python之间进行接口的方法，比如，它们，至少在我上次在那个领域做任何事情的时候，

sentences.en: they're all horrific.
sentences.zh: 它们都很可怕。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to assume that they're, you know, if they're better today, they might be a little bit better, but they're still probably pretty horrific.
sentences.zh: 我只是假设它们，你知道，如果它们今天更好，它们可能会好一点，但它们可能仍然相当可怕。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I'm not a, I'm sure there's, you know, 10% of our listeners are better people to ask for the answer, but, like, in my mental model, C is a much simpler language.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不是，我相信有，你知道，我们10%的听众是更好的询问对象，但是，在我的思维模型中，C是一种简单得多的语言。

sentences.en: That doesn't necessarily, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那不一定，是的。

sentences.en: It doesn't necessarily mean it's a better language, but it is much simpler, like, there's no facilities for, you know, generics or an equivalent of templates.
sentences.zh: 这不一定意味着它是一种更好的语言，但它确实简单得多，比如，没有设施，你知道，泛型或模板的等价物。

sentences.en: And also the evolution of C, although it is ongoing and they are adding things and there is a C committee that is active, I think they are much,
sentences.zh: 而且C的演变，虽然它正在进行中，而且他们正在添加东西，并且有一个活跃的C委员会，我认为他们要，

sentences.en: much more conservative in the language changes that they make.
sentences.zh: 要保守得多，在他们所做的语言更改方面。

sentences.en: And that leads to a much more stable target for an FFI in terms of, like, if something is getting updated, you know,
sentences.zh: 这导致了FFI的一个更稳定的目标，比如，如果有什么东西正在更新，你知道，

sentences.en: every three years with a bunch of new language changes in terms of, like, lambdas and stuff like that, then you, you're going to have people saying, oh, you know,
sentences.zh: 每三年就会有一堆新的语言变化，比如lambda之类的东西，那么你，你就会有人说，哦，你知道，

sentences.en: I want to be able to target this library that uses X.
sentences.zh: 我想能够以使用X的这个库为目标。

sentences.en: But I can't do that now because the FFI capabilities of the language that I'm using doesn't support the new, you know, C11 standard or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但我现在做不到，因为我使用的语言的FFI能力不支持新的，你知道，C11标准之类的东西。

sentences.en: Whether or not that's actually the right answer, I don't actually know, but in my head, that's what it is.
sentences.zh: 无论这是否真的是正确答案，我其实不知道，但在我脑海里，就是这样。

sentences.en: My gut reaction was simplicity, too.
sentences.zh: 我的直觉反应也是简单。

sentences.en: But I suspect that there's something deeper there because there are other languages that are simple, right?
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑其中有更深层的东西，因为还有其他简单的语言，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: perhaps part of it is C's dominance in systems programming for so long that because it was a simple language and because it was the language that platform APIs tend to be written in terms of pretty much every language had to interface with it.
sentences.zh: 也许部分原因是C在系统编程中长期占据主导地位，因为它是简单的语言，而且因为它是平台API倾向于用它编写的语言，几乎每种语言都必须与它进行接口。

sentences.en: And so it just sort of became the de facto standard and maybe simplicity isn't really why it won as the lingua franca, as you said, but maybe it was just early market dominance.
sentences.zh: 所以它就成了事实上的标准，也许简单并不是它作为通用语获胜的真正原因，正如你所说，但也许只是早期的市场主导地位。

sentences.en: Certainly, I think if we talk about why C++ is not a good interface language, the answer is lack of simplicity.
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为如果我们谈论为什么C++不是一种好的接口语言，答案是缺乏简单性。

sentences.en: C++ has a fairly complex type system and template system and that type system gets exposed directly in the spelling of symbols,
sentences.zh: C++有一个相当复杂的类型系统和模板系统，而那个类型系统直接暴露在符号的拼写中，

sentences.en: in functions and in types that other languages would have to interface with.
sentences.zh: 在函数和类型中，其他语言必须与之进行接口。

sentences.en: And to interface to a C++ object, you have to deal with polymorphism, with C++'s way of doing polymorphism, to interface with C++ functions,
sentences.zh: 要与C++对象进行接口，你必须处理多态性，用C++处理多态性的方式，要与C++函数进行接口，

sentences.en: or rather to interface with what we in the C++ world would see as a function, which may include multiple different overloads of the same name.
sentences.zh: 或者更确切地说，要与我们在C++世界中视为函数的东西进行接口，这可能包括同一名称的多个不同重载。

sentences.en: C++, you know, if you're in a language that doesn't have a notion of overloading, each one of those may be a different function.
sentences.zh: C++，你知道，如果你处于一种没有重载概念的语言中，每一个都可能是一个不同的函数。

sentences.en: And if you're in a language that does have some notion of overloading, then you still, like your notion of overloading may be different than C++'s notion of overloading.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你处于一种确实有某种重载概念的语言中，那么你仍然，比如你的重载概念可能与C++的重载概念不同。

sentences.en: And so it's, like, if you look at a simpler question, it's like, what is a function?
sentences.zh: 所以，比如，如果你看一个更简单的问题，就像，什么是函数？

sentences.en: And C is a very simple, straightforward answer.
sentences.zh: 而C是一个非常简单、直接的答案。

sentences.en: C++, I would argue, does not have a simple, straightforward answer to that.
sentences.zh: C++，我会说，对这个问题没有一个简单、直接的答案。

sentences.en: Because what we as C++ programmers think of as a function might actually be really a function template or an overloaded, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为我们作为C++程序员认为的函数实际上可能真的是一个函数模板或一个重载的，你知道，

sentences.en: function that boils down to multiple different actual function entry points in the, you know, the binary ABI representation that other languages would have to interface with.
sentences.zh: 函数，它归结为二进制ABI表示中的多个不同的实际函数入口点，其他语言必须与之进行接口。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So certainly lack of simplicity is why C++ is not the lingua franqua.
sentences.zh: 所以当然缺乏简单性是C++不是通用语的原因。

sentences.en: But is simplicity really the key thing that makes C the lingua franqua?
sentences.zh: 但简单性真的是使C成为通用语的关键吗？

sentences.en: Perhaps it's the nature of the C type system, where you have these sort of fuzzy-sized types.
sentences.zh: 也许是C类型系统的本质，你有这些模糊大小的类型。

sentences.en: Maybe it's...
sentences.zh: 也许是……

sentences.en: I think what you said earlier is a huge component of it, though.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你刚才说的是其中的一个巨大组成部分。

sentences.en: Like, C has a 50-year head start, and maybe a language like Zig is actually a better language to target as an FFI target.
sentences.zh: 比如，C有50年的领先优势，也许像Zig这样的语言实际上是作为FFI目标更好的语言。

sentences.en: But Zig is created in the last 10 years, and there's not, like,
sentences.zh: 但Zig是过去10年里创建的，而且没有，比如，

sentences.en: I don't know what the number of libraries that are designed in C or system libraries that were designed either because they were designed decades ago or they were recently designed,
sentences.zh: 我不知道有多少库是用C设计的，或者系统库是因为它们几十年前设计的，或者是最近设计的，

sentences.en: but they wanted to be good targets for FFI.
sentences.zh: 但它们想成为FFI的好目标。

sentences.en: So it's just, like, because it's, what is it, like, the rich gets richer?
sentences.zh: 所以这只是，比如，因为它是什么，比如，富者越富？

sentences.en: Like, they had a 50-year head start, and there are probably languages out there or languages that could be designed that would be better targets,
sentences.zh: 比如，它们有50年的领先优势，而且可能存在可以设计出来的更好的语言，

sentences.en: but they don't have a 50-year head start, and they don't have the ecosystem of languages.
sentences.zh: 但它们没有50年的领先优势，也没有语言的生态系统。

sentences.en: The answer here really may be, not to compare C to contemporary languages, but really to ask ourselves, if we turn the clock back, we go back to the 70s,
sentences.zh: 这里的答案可能真的不是将C与当代语言进行比较，而是真正问自己，如果我们把时钟拨回，回到70年代，

sentences.en: what really made C successful compared to its contemporary languages?
sentences.zh: 与当时的当代语言相比，是什么真正使C成功了？

sentences.en: And specifically, what made it successful as the systems programming language?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是什么使它作为系统编程语言成功了？

sentences.en: And this is not a question that is an unknown question.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个未知的问题。

sentences.en: It's been talked about, perhaps even talked about to death in other podcasts, other literature, other mediuMs.
sentences.zh: 它已经被讨论过了，甚至在其他播客、其他文献、其他媒体中被讨论到烂了。

sentences.en: I mean, wait, though, what were the other systems languages at the time?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，等等，当时还有什么其他系统语言？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I personally, I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我个人，我一点头绪都没有。

sentences.en: I don't know either.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, the only one I can think of is Ada, and I actually don't know what year that was created.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我唯一能想到的是Ada，而且我其实不知道那是哪一年创建的。

sentences.en: And I can rattle you off a bunch of other popular languages from the 70s and 80s, like Smalltalk and Pascal and et cetera, but like none of those were systems languages.
sentences.zh: 我还能随口说出一堆70和80年代流行的其他语言，比如Smalltalk、Pascal等等，但它们都不是系统级语言。

sentences.en: Ada and Smalltalk, or sorry, yeah, Ada and Smalltalk, I think, let's talk about those briefly, because I think they have some similarities there.
sentences.zh: Ada和Smalltalk，或者抱歉，对，Ada和Smalltalk，我想我们简要谈谈它们，因为我觉得它们之间有一些相似之处。

sentences.en: Ada and Smalltalk?
sentences.zh: Ada和Smalltalk？

sentences.en: In comparison to C.
sentences.zh: 与C语言相比。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, they're very dissimilar languages, though, correct?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们是非常不同的语言，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, but in terms of level of complexity.
sentences.zh: 是的，但在复杂程度方面。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They both have, do they both have an object model?
sentences.zh: 它们都有，它们都有对象模型吗？

sentences.en: I know Ada does now, did it back in the day.
sentences.zh: 我知道Ada现在有了，以前有没有我就不知道了。

sentences.en: I know very little about Ada, other than what it's, it's one of the very few languages that has fixed point and bounded integer types as a part of their type system.
sentences.zh: 我对Ada知之甚少，只知道它是极少数将定点数和有界整数类型作为类型系统一部分的语言之一。

sentences.en: I mean, Smalltalk certainly was an object-oriented language from the start, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，Smalltalk从一开始肯定就是一种面向对象的语言，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实如此。

sentences.en: And, okay.
sentences.zh: 而且，好吧。

sentences.en: It is the.
sentences.zh: 它是。

sentences.en: I'm fairly certain, just based on the first sentence of the Ada wiki, that it's also an object-oriented programming language from the start.
sentences.zh: 我相当确定，仅从Ada维基百科的第一句话来看，它从一开始也是一种面向对象的编程语言。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Is Pascal, was Pascal, is Pascal an object-oriented language?
sentences.zh: Pascal是，曾经是，Pascal是面向对象语言吗？

sentences.en: Hmm, I don't know much about Pascal, other than it was one of Verth's languages.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对Pascal了解不多，只知道它是沃思（Wirth）的语言之一。

sentences.en: Because, isn't there object Pascal, which was a later derivative of it, specifically for object-oriented programming?
sentences.zh: 因为不是有Object Pascal吗？那是后来衍生出来的，专门用于面向对象编程的。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: I know that Pascal led to Delphi, or Delphi.
sentences.zh: 我知道Pascal衍生出了Delphi。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I would say that the reason that Ada and Smalltalk probably didn't succeed as a lingua franca.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会说Ada和Smalltalk之所以没能成为通用语言的原因。

sentences.en: Wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: I've got to clear this up.
sentences.zh: 我得澄清一下。

sentences.en: Is the same reason that C++ fails in comparison to C, which is that they're substantially more complex languages, and in particular, they're languages with an object model.
sentences.zh: 和C++相比C语言失败的原因是一样的，那就是它们是复杂得多的语言，特别是它们是有对象模型的语言。

sentences.en: And figuring out how to interface to objects is harder than figuring out how to interface to simple structs and functions.
sentences.zh: 而且弄清楚如何与对象交互比弄清楚如何与简单的结构体和函数交互要难得多。

sentences.en: There's a couple listeners that are, like, screaming in their heads right now, because you've misunderstood what I said.
sentences.zh: 现在有几个听众可能在心里尖叫，因为你误解了我的意思。

sentences.en: I was rattling off a couple popular languages that would never have been the lingua franca FFI target, because they're not systeMs.
sentences.zh: 我刚才随口列举了几种流行的语言，它们永远不会成为通用的FFI目标，因为它们不是系统级语言。

sentences.en: Like, Smalltalk is, like, a totally GC'd, not the most performant message-passing system that lives in, like, a workspace similar to APL, that, like, you don't have, like,
sentences.zh: 比如，Smalltalk是一个完全垃圾回收的、性能不是最优的消息传递系统，它存在于类似于APL的工作区中，你没有，比如，

sentences.en: written text.
sentences.zh: 书面文本。

sentences.en: You have, like, workspaces that you load, and so, and, like, you can only develop in Smalltalk in, like, a specific IDE that's built for the language.
sentences.zh: 你有的是加载的工作区，所以，而且，你只能在为该语言构建的特定IDE中开发Smalltalk。

sentences.en: Like, it would be impossible.
sentences.zh: 这简直是不可能的。

sentences.en: You know, and I get that, and I was confused while you were listening to that, but Ada is different.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我明白这一点，你在听的时候我感到困惑，但Ada不同。

sentences.en: So, yeah, Ada is.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，Ada是。

sentences.en: It's, that's, that was the only, so I said, the only systems language that I know that might be a contender would be Ada, but, like,
sentences.zh: 它是，那是，那是唯一一个，所以我说，我知道的唯一可能成为竞争者的系统级语言是Ada，但是，

sentences.en: all the other languages I know wouldn't be contenders, because I don't think, like, a GC would.
sentences.zh: 我所知道的其他所有语言都不会是竞争者，因为我不认为垃圾回收机制能行。

sentences.en: I think, you know, I think, I think Pascoe's actually, I think, I think the question is really, why did, because Pascoe is the contemporary of C, right?
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我想，我想Pascal实际上，我想，我想问题真的是，为什么，因为Pascal是C的同代语言，对吧？

sentences.en: I think the question is, like, why C not Pascoe?
sentences.zh: 我想问题是，为什么是C而不是Pascal？

sentences.en: I mean, Pascoe wasn't very popular.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，Pascal当时并不太流行。

sentences.en: Like, Pascoe.
sentences.zh: 比如，Pascal。

sentences.en: Yeah, but why not?
sentences.zh: 是的，但为什么不呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not an expert in Pascoe, we'd have to have someone on, but, like, the high-level things that I know about Pascoe are that, is that it was taught a lot in schools,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不是Pascal专家，我们得请人来讲讲，但我对Pascal了解的高层信息是，它在学校里教得很多，

sentences.en: there were a bunch of people that really liked it, but at the end of the day, from, like, a programming language theory point of view, like,
sentences.zh: 有一群人真的很喜欢它，但归根结底，从编程语言理论的角度来看，

sentences.en: they introduced a lot of interesting concepts that then other languages adopted, but, like, it had these fatal flaws that made it very difficult to, like,
sentences.zh: 它们引入了许多有趣的理念，后来被其他语言采纳了，但它有一些致命的缺陷，使得它很难，比如，

sentences.en: build large-scale programs and, like, really be productive in.
sentences.zh: 构建大规模程序，并且很难真正提高生产力。

sentences.en: And what those are, I do not know.
sentences.zh: 至于具体是什么，我不知道。

sentences.en: If you are a Pascoe person, feel free to leave a comment on Twitter or a comment on our GitHub discussion in the podcast notes.
sentences.zh: 如果你是Pascal用户，欢迎在Twitter上留言，或者在播客笔记的GitHub讨论区发表评论。

sentences.en: But I just know that, like, Pascoe was an interesting language, it had a certain, in its heyday, a modicum of success,
sentences.zh: 但我只知道，Pascal是一门有趣的语言，在它的鼎盛时期，它确实取得了一定的成功，

sentences.en: but no one was really surprised at the end of the day when it didn't, like, thrive.
sentences.zh: 但当它最终没能繁荣发展时，没有人感到真正惊讶。

sentences.en: I think.
sentences.zh: 我想。

sentences.en: I could be wrong.
sentences.zh: 我也可能错了。

sentences.en: I'm sort of, like I said, high-level from what I know.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我只是从我所知道的高层角度来看。

sentences.en: Pascoe is a language I know very little about compared to small talk.
sentences.zh: 与Smalltalk相比，我对Pascal了解甚少。

sentences.en: Well, I'm, like, at risk of offending some more of the listener.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我冒着得罪更多听众的风险。

sentences.en: We've got to have some old person on here to teach us some things about the history of C.
sentences.zh: 我们得请一位老前辈来教我们一些关于C语言历史的知识。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, we've got to have a lot of folks on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们得请很多人来。

sentences.en: I mean, we've got a couple comments that said you have to get Brian Cantrell on as, like, fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们收到几条评论说你必须尽快请到Brian Cantrell。

sentences.en: So, I don't think Brian listens to this, but we will reach out to Brian.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不认为Brian会听这个，但我们会联系他。

sentences.en: I mean, we've, I think we have a list of folks that we, I mean, we still have a long list of folks from when we talked to Jane,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们，我想我们有一份名单，我们，我的意思是，我们还有一份很长的名单，那是我们和Jane交谈时留下的，

sentences.en: which was the start and then very quick end of our Us Becoming a Rust podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 那是我们成为Rust播客的开始，也是非常迅速的结束。

sentences.en: But we were supposed to have a bunch of folks on, Esteban, who worked a lot on the error messages.
sentences.zh: 但我们本应邀请很多人，比如Esteban，他在错误消息方面做了很多工作。

sentences.en: We were supposed to have JT on to talk about, you know, the working on the community aspect of Rust and why it became super successful.
sentences.zh: 我们本应邀请JT来谈谈，你知道，关于Rust的社区建设以及它为何如此成功。

sentences.en: Anyways, lots of folks.
sentences.zh: 总之，很多人。

sentences.en: And we will also have someone who is a C expert and a C.
sentences.zh: 我们也会邀请一位C语言专家。

sentences.en: I was thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Is veteran a word that you should not be using?
sentences.zh: “老兵”（veteran）这个词是不是不该用？

sentences.en: Because I referred to a, in a couple talks, I said that I referred to APL people that I chatted with as these APL veterans.
sentences.zh: 因为我提到过，在几次谈话中，我把和我聊天的APL用户称为“APL老兵”。

sentences.en: And in hindsight, I was like, I probably should have just said experts.
sentences.zh: 事后看来，我觉得我可能应该直接说“专家”。

sentences.en: But I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 但我不太确定。

sentences.en: Is it on a list of words or is it okay to say veteran?
sentences.zh: 它在禁用词汇表里吗？还是说“老兵”这个词是可以用的？

sentences.en: It's not on the list of words that I worked on, the incising because of terminology liSt.
sentences.zh: 它不在我参与制定的术语禁用列表中。

sentences.en: However, there are words in that list that are words that I recommended avoiding because they were military jargon or they had a military connotation.
sentences.zh: 不过，列表中确实有一些词是我建议避免使用的，因为它们是军事术语或带有军事色彩。

sentences.en: I generally think that it's best to avoid words that have any sort of military or war connotation if you can.
sentences.zh: 我通常认为，如果可以的话，最好避免使用任何带有军事或战争色彩的词汇。

sentences.en: And I know that there are some people that are bothered by it.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些人对此感到困扰。

sentences.en: The nice thing about the word veteran is I actually think it encapsulates a certain amount of respect because you're trying to say not only are you an expert,
sentences.zh: “老兵”这个词的好处在于，我实际上认为它包含了一定程度的尊重，因为你不仅是在说你是专家，

sentences.en: but you're an expert that has been doing this for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且你是一位长期从事该领域的专家。

sentences.en: So it's both like experience and expertise.
sentences.zh: 所以它既包含经验，也包含专业知识。

sentences.en: And I don't know, like expert covers 60% of that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，专家这个词只能涵盖其中的60%。

sentences.en: I don't think anyone is going to be like, oh, you're just calling me an expert.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有人会觉得，哦，你只是叫我专家。

sentences.en: I would prefer you point out that I've been doing this for decades.
sentences.zh: 我更希望你指出我已经在这个领域做了几十年了。

sentences.en: But anyways, yeah, probably best to.
sentences.zh: 但总之，是的，可能最好还是……

sentences.en: I would avoid the term veteran because it does have a military connotation.
sentences.zh: 我会避免使用“老兵”这个词，因为它确实带有军事色彩。

sentences.en: However, I did take two years of college Latin and I learned very little, but very, very little.
sentences.zh: 不过，我在大学里修过两年拉丁语，学到的东西很少，非常非常少。

sentences.en: I took Latin in college because I figured it's a dead language.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里修拉丁语是因为我觉得它是一门死语言。

sentences.en: They can't make you speak it.
sentences.zh: 他们没法强迫你开口说。

sentences.en: Like they would make you write it, but I was like, they can't make me speak it and I'm terrible at pronouncing things.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会强迫你写，但我想，他们没法强迫我开口说，而且我发音很糟糕。

sentences.en: I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我错了。

sentences.en: They made me try to pronounce Latin.
sentences.zh: 他们强迫我尝试发音拉丁语。

sentences.en: I'm pretty certain that veteran comes from the Latin, the turnus, the turnus, something like that, which is, which means like old,
sentences.zh: 我相当确定“veteran”来自拉丁语“veternus”之类的词，意思是“老”，

sentences.en: like experienced and does not have a specific military connotation.
sentences.zh: 像“有经验的”，并没有特定的军事含义。

sentences.en: I think the origin of the word doesn't have that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个词的起源并没有那种含义。

sentences.en: But since then, you know, culturally, we, we, you say veteran, um, uh, you assume that people mean, uh, people hear a military connotation to it.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，你知道，在文化上，我们，当你提到“老兵”，嗯，你会假设人们的意思是，嗯，人们听到了军事色彩。

sentences.en: So that's why we should avoid it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们应该避免使用它的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, I, now, right after I said, you know, it doesn't capture the experience part, um, only the expert part by saying expert.
